what_its_for: Galantamine is used to treat mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. It helps improve memory, thinking, and daily functioning by boosting the levels of a natural chemical in the brain called acetylcholine. It does not cure Alzheimer's disease, but it can help slow down the worsening of symptoms.
how_to_take: Take galantamine exactly as your doctor prescribed. Immediate-release tablets and oral solution are taken TWICE a day, preferably with breakfast and dinner. Extended-release capsules are taken ONCE a day in the morning, with food. Swallow extended-release capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. If you use the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided. Drink a full glass of water with each dose. Always take this medicine with food to help reduce stomach upset.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and gradually increase it over several weeks to reduce side effects. The typical starting dose is 8 mg per day, which may be increased to 16 mg per day after at least 4 weeks, and then up to 24 mg per day if needed and tolerated. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If you forget for an entire day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule the next day. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store galantamine tablets and extended-release capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the oral solution at room temperature and do not freeze it. Keep all forms of this medication in a dry place, away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking galantamine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Be careful when driving, operating machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because some medicines can interact with galantamine. Avoid starting or stopping any medication without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fainting or slow heartbeat, severe vomiting or diarrhea leading to dehydration, difficulty urinating or painful urination, seizures, shortness of breath or wheezing, signs of stomach bleeding such as vomiting blood or dark/tarry stools, muscle weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms, significant weight loss, or if side effects like nausea or dizziness do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Galantamine may take several weeks before you notice any benefit. Most people begin to see some improvement in memory or daily functioning after 4 to 12 weeks of treatment. Remember, this medication works best when taken consistently every day. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel it is not helping — stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to get worse more quickly.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution as side effects like dizziness and falls may be more likely. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or avoid this medication entirely if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease — always inform your doctor of any kidney or liver issues. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have a slow heartbeat, heart block, or other heart rhythm problems, as galantamine can affect your heart rate. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: The safety of galantamine during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not well established. Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
